title: application-core objects O2: the regression harness compares the two versions' constructor admission; lib/tests/integration.rs and the record and object examples under it
description: Row O2 of llm-dlc/loops/application-core-acceptance.md, the negative control of a narrower new constructor under an anchored domain. At this revision the regression harness (lib/src/harness/mod.rs, generate_in and its Java rendering) makes the new version's objects, then the previous version's, in separate handler regions: an input both versions' constructors reject is skipped as before, one that only one version's reject is now a difference (an AssertionError), where every object is made in both versions of the same shape (Layout::compares_admission). Before, an input either constructor rejected was skipped, so a narrower constructor was silently intersected. Verified inline on the native engine (tests/application_core_objects.rs). This job checks the same harness under JBMC and that the existing examples keep their verdicts: every record/object harness now has two construction regions and the previous version's construction emitted twice, so JBMC's formula changes even where the constructors are identical. Engine: as each example's build.py and the integration tests choose (JBMC and native); bounds as recorded per example.
expected: integration tests: every non-ignored test passes (exit 0). Each example's build.py prints 'as expected' and exits 0, its verdict unchanged: 126 violation, 127 verified, 128 violation, 129 verified, 130 violation, 131 verified, 134 violation, 135 verified, 136 violation, 137 verified, 150 verified, 151 violation, 152 verified, 190 verified, 191-194 violation, 195 verified, 196 unverifiable. Only the statement's constructible-assumption text may change, where admission is compared. A changed verdict is a finding, not a pass.
